rationale: Self-review against the reported diagnoses indicates the reusable guidance has already been repaired in the current skill bundle:

1) Workflow 2 now explicitly requires defining completion via a domain-sourced terminal-event predicate, forbids EOF/boundedness as a per-key completion signal, and mandates event-time-safe finalization by delaying emission until the watermark passes a safe point beyond the terminal timestamp.

2) The Semantic Contract Gate list is correctly structured and numbered as three separate predicates (contributing-event, completion/terminal-event, output-eligibility), with additional reusable operationalization rules (multiple terminal events determinism, eligibility controlled only by contributing activity).

3) The temporary task guidance no longer recommends emitting (jobId, 0) by default for keys without qualifying activity; it aligns with the Non-negotiable Flink Emission Gate and conditions empty-output behavior on explicit task requirements.
residual_risks: Terminal-event types remain domain/dataset dependent; implementers must still consult the dataset spec to enumerate terminal job lifecycle events and document the chosen deterministic rule for multiple terminal signals (e.g., first terminal wins).

The “safe point” delay (terminal_ts + allowed lateness/out-of-orderness bound) requires an explicit lateness/bound assumption; if not stated by the source system, implementations may need conservative defaults and corresponding tests/fixtures.

If downstream evaluations expect explicit zero rows for lifecycle-only keys (contrary to the emission gate), tasks must state this explicitly; otherwise the default should remain “no row for no qualifying activity.”
